items.title: Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy - CBS News
items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.

items.title: What is the Future of Journalism in the World of TikTok and AI
items.summary:
Audio, video and podcasts are now a regular part of the storytelling process. According to the Reuters 2026 Digital News Report, 77% of people around the world watch online news weekly. AI chatbots are the “new frontier,” with 10% of audiences turning to them for news updates, compared to 7% last year, the report found.

 Kathleen Kingsbury laughs while talking with two attendees at the lecture. [...] The New York Times makes it possible by having communication teams across the globe. “We run a 24/7 news operation, and we’ve had to get very, very good about collaboration,” she said.

Kingsbury also told the audience that she is optimistic about using AI “as a tool” and as a resource for digging into large data sets. [...] Northeastern journalism professor Meg Heckman asked Kingsbury about the craft of journalism and the stakes currently facing the industry, inquiring how her publication is managing to reach audiences given that the dearth of advertising dollars has forced many news outlets, including the NYT, to put its content behind a paywall to drive subscriptions. This can make it more challenging to draw readers, who also now have the option to consult AI for news updates.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \(x^2\) là:

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

**Giải thích nhanh:** Áp dụng công thức nguyên hàm cơ bản \(\int x^n \, dx = \dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C\) với \(n = 2\):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \(C\) là hằng số tích phân.

**Kiểm tra lại:** Đạo hàm của \(\dfrac{x^3}{3} + C\) là \(\dfrac{3x^2}{3} = x^2\) ✓

Bạn có muốn mình giải thêm bài tích phân nào khác không?

result.actual_text:
Chào bạn! Mình là trợ lý nghiên cứu thông tin — tập trung vào việc thu thập, tra cứu và tổng hợp dữ liệu từ các nguồn bên ngoài. Cụ thể mình làm được những việc sau:

**1. Tra cứu & tìm kiếm thông tin**
- Tra cứu thông tin trên internet (tin tức hoặc kiến thức chung), có lọc theo khoảng thời gian (ngày/tuần/tháng/năm).
- Tìm kiếm trên mạng xã hội (sắp xếp theo mới nhất hoặc nổi bật nhất).
- Đọc các bài đăng gần đây từ một tài khoản mạng xã hội cụ thể.

**2. Nghiên cứu học thuật**
- Tìm bài báo khoa học theo từ khóa.
- Đọc nội dung chi tiết của một bài báo (theo ID hoặc đường dẫn arXiv).

**3. Đọc & xử lý nội dung**
- Lấy nội dung từ một địa chỉ web cụ thể.
- Tra cứu tài liệu nội bộ (chính sách về nghiên cứu AI, trích dẫn nguồn, quyền riêng tư dữ liệu, xuất bản nội dung, sử dụng công cụ).
- Trình bày/tổng hợp dữ liệu đã có thành văn bản theo nhiều khuôn mẫu khác nhau (ngắn gọn, theo mục, bullet, thread...).

**4. Hỗ trợ gửi nội dung**
- Gửi/publish văn bản đi (sẽ luôn hỏi xác nhận trước khi gửi).

**Một vài lưu ý về cách mình làm việc:**
- Nếu bạn nhờ đọc một đường link mà chưa đưa URL hợp lệ, mình sẽ hỏi lại thay vì tự đoán.
- Nếu bạn muốn xem bài đăng/timeline mà chưa nêu tên tài khoản, mình sẽ hỏi lại.
- Với các việc ngoài phạm vi nghiên cứu (ví dụ lập trình, kiến thức chung), mình sẽ trả lời trực tiếp bằng văn bản.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

[...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.summary:

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said.
